headline: High: agent_a’s broad egress and browser/tooling can leak or act on agent_b outputs; prompt-injection and data-flow risks are otherwise mostly undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and use runtime-injected MCPs/hooks, so it may ingest untrusted content from agent_b or shared channels. agent_b is a data-engineering system with no documented isolation or provenance controls. The pairwise bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a consumes agent_b-produced text from a shared file, queue, or MCP channel without provenance checks, injection is plausible.
IF an orchestrator bridges agent_b outputs into agent_a browser or subprocess prompts, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of agent_b outputs into agent_a prompts.
Add provenance tags to any shared messages or files.
Require a human review step before agent_a acts on agent_b content.
Restrict agent_a browser access to trusted domains only.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches provider auth data, session history, project code, and broad network egress; agent_b has no documented egress and no data classes listed. If they share a workspace or credentials, agent_a can exfiltrate sensitive material, but the pairwise sharing path is not documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or credential store, agent_a can transmit those contents off-host.
IF agent_b writes sensitive data into paths readable by agent_a, leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct OS users.
Remove shared credential files from any common workspace.
Block agent_a egress except to approved endpoints.
Rotate any provider auth data exposed to agent_a.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can write files and spawn subprocesses, while agent_b exposes no write or concurrency surfaces in the profile. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so a direct capability conflict is not established; only a small coordination risk remains if an external orchestrator shares state.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable task state, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Make shared files read-only for one agent.
Check for lockfiles before edits.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency or locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate browser- and tool-mediated outputs, and agent_b is a data-engineering system that may consume upstream results. If agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream data work. The profiles do not document verification gates, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a-produced text or artifacts without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF agent_a’s outputs are used as inputs to transformations or materialized views, downstream errors can multiply.
mitigations: Require schema validation on agent_a outputs before agent_b uses them.
Insert a human approval step for high-impact actions.
Log and diff agent_a outputs against source data.
Limit agent_b to read-only consumption of agent_a artifacts until verified.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles provider auth prompts and session history, while agent_b lists no sensitive data classes or residency constraints. No explicit compliance mismatch is documented, so only a low-risk gap exists if regulated data is introduced into agent_a’s broader egress environment.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed into agent_a’s session history or auth prompts, retention and residency review is needed.
IF agent_b is later configured to process regulated records, the pair may inherit a policy mismatch.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in agent_a prompts.
Review retention settings for session history.
Keep agent_b on non-regulated datasets unless approved.
Document data-class handling for both agents.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
